The Critical Strategist

Secondary (40%): High Dominance (D) – Adds assertiveness, directness, and drive to enforce standards.

• As a student: Directly enforces project quality and rigor.
• At work: Strategic auditing, risk management.
• In personal life: Systematic, standards-based home management.
• Key strengths: Objective systemic integrity, policy enforcement, logical rigor
• Energised by: System efficiency, technical precision, logical strategies, and clear performance standards.

answers.NONE|what_is_disc:
DISC describes behaviour through four styles:
• Dominant (D) – Decisive, results-oriented, risk-tolerant, high execution velocity; risk of interpersonal friction
• Influential (I) – Persuasive, highly relational, visionary, optimistic; risk of disorganization and overcommitting
• Steady (S) – Supportive, loyal, highly consistent, patient team builders; risk of resisting rapid change
• Compliant (C) – Analytically rigorous, quality-focused, objective systems designers; risk of perfectionism paralysis

Every person has a primary style (60%) and a secondary style (40%), which gives 16 combinations — for example D/I (Dominant primary, Influential secondary).
